[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] DartPoints own site describes a strategy of delivering enterprise grade colocation, cloud, and managed infrastructure services to communities outside the largest United States metros, operating in Tier 2 and Tier 3 regional markets. The company began operations in the early 2000s. DartPoints is headquartered at 1601 Elm Street, Suite 3650, Dallas, Texas. This session refreshed and sharpened a prior research passes brief note that the company received a strategic growth investment from NOVA Infrastructure in 2025: per both DartPoints own press release and independent trade press corroboration from Data Center Dynamics, both fetched fresh this session, NOVA Infrastructure actually acquired majority control of DartPoints, announced April 30, 2025, with lending partner Orion Infrastructure Capital, committing more than 250 million dollars in combined growth capital, while the prior owner, Astra Capital Management, retained a meaningful minority stake. As part of that same transaction, DartPoints acquired the underlying real estate for three of its data centers, in Greenville, South Carolina, Baton Rouge, Louisiana, and Asheville, North Carolina, per both sources. DartPoints own site lists 11 facilities across 10 markets, including Baton Rouge, Louisiana (2 facilities) and Shreveport, Louisiana, Cincinnati and Dublin, Ohio, Columbus, Indiana, Asheville, North Carolina, and Columbia, Greenville, Charleston, and Spartanburg, South Carolina, matching every state where this registry lists a DartPoints facility, and DCD independently corroborates the same 11 facility, 10 market count and adds that the company serves more than 900 enterprise customers including Fortune 500 companies, universities, and hospital systems. The company emphasizes AI ready, high density infrastructure, 99.999 percent uptime, and SOC 2 Type II compliance. This specific row, the Columbus, Indiana facility (internal code CLU01), per the operators own dedicated location page for this facility, fetched fresh this session, sits at 2425 Technology Boulevard, Columbus, IN 47201.
sources_tried: DartPoints own dedicated Columbus location page, DartPoints own NOVA Infrastructure press release, and independent Data Center Dynamics trade press coverage of the same transaction

reading:
DartPoints is a privately held colocation operator headquartered at 1601 Elm Street, Suite 3650, Dallas, Texas, founded in the early 2000s. NOVA Infrastructure made a strategic growth investment in the company in 2025.

The company positions itself explicitly around secondary markets, describing its mission as bringing enterprise-grade colocation, cloud, and managed infrastructure to communities outside the largest US metros, with an emphasis on AI-ready, high-density capacity supporting regional economic growth. Its operator site lists 11 facilities across Indiana, Louisiana, North Carolina, Ohio, and South Carolina, naming Columbus, Indiana, Baton Rouge and Shreveport, Louisiana, Asheville, North Carolina, Cincinnati and Dublin, Ohio, and Columbia, Charleston, Greenville, and Spartanburg, South Carolina.

The registry here tracks 10 DartPoints facilities across four states, Indiana, Louisiana, Ohio, and South Carolina, closely matching the operator's own named markets, with North Carolina the one state named on the operator's site not reflected among this registry's current DartPoints rows. As an explicitly Tier 2/Tier 3-focused operator, DartPoints stands apart from the metro-core colocation model of Equinix and CoreSite and the hyperscaler campus model of AWS and Meta recorded elsewhere in this registry, representing smaller-market colocation demand rather than large-scale AI training capacity.
